Subject: Exploring private offer term length & buyer approval flow

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the predictable inference latency numbers. Procurement and IT asked me to confirm a couple of constraints before we move the private offer to our legal queue:

- MedSys prefers a 9-month pilot PO (starts Jan 1) rather than a full 12 months — procurement wants ability to re-evaluate at business Q3. Is Redwood able to support a 9-month private offer on AWS Marketplace?
- Our procurement process requires a two-stage approval: centralized procurement + IT security signoff, then the business unit (Clinical AI) does a separate budget release. Can we express multiple buyer signoffs in the PO or do we need separate offers?
- Any implications for co-sell eligibility / pricing tiers if we shorten term length?

I'm attaching the SOW for scope. If you can outline the typical sequencing and any gating we should expect on Redwood's side (legal, pricing approvers, marketplace ops), that would be helpful to have before our internal kickoff on Friday.

Thanks,
Laura

Hi Laura — great to hear the demo landed well. Appreciate the SOW — read through it and added a short pricing grid for options (attached). High level answers and a recommended sequencing below.

Summary answers:
- 9-month private offer: Yes, we can list a private offer for a 9-month term on AWS Marketplace. Note: Marketplace reporting/proration works off the offer duration; for a shorter term we typically recommend prorated billing to match buyer expectations.
- Multi-stage approval (procurement + IT + business): AWS private offers support a single purchaser entity per PO, but you can represent multi-stakeholder approvals in the procurement process outside of AWS (we provide a co-sell-ready contract template and can add an approval checklist to the offer metadata). Practically we handle this two ways:
  1) Single private offer for MedSys (recommended) + an internal "buyer gating" checklist you provide that we mirror in our onboarding playbook; or
  2) If your legal requires separate legal signoffs per business unit, we can create sequential offers but that adds operational overhead.
- Co-sell eligibility & pricing: Shorter terms generally reduce the discount window — to preserve co-sell incentives we can keep the same list price but adjust the committed usage threshold. For example, a 9-month pilot could have a slightly higher effective MSPR with the same co-sell credit. I captured two scenarios in the attached pricing-grid.

Recommended next steps (mutual action plan):
1) You share the internal approver list + expected approval cadence (names/email/roles) — we will mirror this in HubSpot and AWS offer comments.
2) Redwood (Vanessa) routes a private offer draft to AWS Marketplace ops for verification (1-2 business days).
3) Redwood legal (Vivek) reviews the standard co-sell addendum; we target a 48-hour turn.
4) Sign PO in DocuSign + AWS private offer acceptance.

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT to walk procurement/IT through the checklist? If that works I'll loop in Vanessa who runs marketplace ops for us.

Cheers,
Soojin

Vanessa / Vivek — quick internal note pulled into thread so MedSys sees the progress. Key asks:

- Pricing ask: MedSys prefers a 9-month pilot. I'm proposing a 12% co-sell discount band for the 9-month pilot (effective price in the attached sheet). Vanessa, can you confirm Marketplace ops can publish a 9-month single private offer with proration and a DocuSign sign flow?
- Legal ask: Vivek, we may need a 48-hour review on the co-sell addendum; MedSys legal tends to redline the data retention clause.
- Timeline: MedSys requested an internal kickoff Friday; if we lock pricing tomorrow we can route to AWS and have the offer published early next week.

If either of you prefer a different discount band I can push back to procurement. My judgment: keep co-sell incentive visible (12% works) but hold the deeper volume credits for a 12-month commit upsell later.

Thanks — looping Laura to keep visibility.
